goals: Quantify hillslope-to-stream travel times across topographic positions
Resolve lateral subsurface flow convergence along flowpaths
Represent groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
key_processes: lateral subsurface flow along topographic gradients
travel time tracking through the hillslope-stream continuum
drivers_to_resolve: soil hydraulic properties (controlling lateral flow rates)

model_choice.rationale: The brief specifies 'site' archetype, but ELM single-column is fundamentally incapable of the requested lateral transport physics. A lateral flow model (ParFlow, PFLOTRAN 3-D, or coupled framework) is required.
model_choice.coupling_note: The question requires either (1) a 2-D/3-D lateral flow model (ParFlow or PFLOTRAN transient 3-D) that natively represents hillslope convergence and inter-column exchange, OR (2) ELM coupled to a hillslope routing/travel-time framework. Neither exists in the current stack. Listed under requires_capabilities.

answerable: Vertical water partitioning differences by topographic position (ridge vs valley) — but as independent 1-D columns, not connected by lateral flow
Elevation/climate gradients across the basin (via NLDAS 12 km forcing)
Soil texture control on vertical drainage (per-column SSURGO)

not_answerable.why: ELM single-column has no travel time tracking or age tracer mechanism
not_answerable.needs: Travel time tracer or post-processing routing tool with age tracking

not_answerable.aspect: Lateral subsurface flow convergence along topographic flowpaths
not_answerable.why: ELM columns are independent 1-D vertical; no lateral flow between columns
not_answerable.needs: 2-D/3-D lateral flow model (ParFlow, PFLOTRAN 3-D transient, or ELM-ParFlow coupling)

not_answerable.aspect: Groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
not_answerable.why: No inter-column communication in single-column ELM; each column has an isolated 1-D water table
not_answerable.needs: Lateral groundwater flow model or coupled hillslope framework

not_answerable.aspect: Integrated streamflow at outlet (to define stream arrival)
not_answerable.why: No native routing; columns do not aggregate to a stream network
not_answerable.needs: Routing model or post-processing aggregation tool

sampling_strategy.approach: Not applicable — the question's primary mechanism (lateral flow and inter-column exchange) cannot be represented by the current single-column stack. A stratified ELM column set would produce independent 1-D responses, not travel times or lateral connectivity.
sampling_strategy.n_justification: Zero columns designed because the execution stack cannot answer the question as posed. Designing a column set would misrepresent the framework's capabilities.

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: Not applicable — no experiment designed due to infeasibility

requires_capabilities.capability: 2-D or 3-D lateral subsurface flow model (ParFlow, PFLOTRAN 3-D transient, or equivalent)
requires_capabilities.why: The question's core mechanism is lateral flow convergence along hillslope flowpaths and inter-column groundwater exchange, which single-column ELM cannot represent
requires_capabilities.blocks: All three goals: travel times, lateral convergence, and inter-column exchange

requires_capabilities.capability: Hillslope routing / travel time tracking framework
requires_capabilities.why: To compute travel times from hillslope positions to stream outlet, either natively in a lateral flow model or as a post-processing tool
If the intent is to use ELM for land surface processes and couple to a lateral flow model for subsurface transport
requires_capabilities.blocks: Integrated hillslope-stream simulation with ELM land surface physics

requires_capabilities.capability: Stream network / outlet definition for the Naches HUC8
requires_capabilities.why: To define the 'stream' endpoint for travel time calculations

requires_capabilities.capability: Age tracer or particle tracking in subsurface flow model
requires_capabilities.why: To explicitly track water parcels from hillslope origin to stream arrival
requires_capabilities.blocks: Direct travel time computation (alternative: residence time distribution from flux time series)

assumptions: The user request is interpreted literally: hillslope-to-stream travel times require lateral transport and inter-column connectivity, not independent 1-D column responses.
No observations are available for validation (observations_available is empty), so this would be a purely model-based exploration if it were feasible.
The Naches domain has significant topographic relief (352-1977 m), which would drive lateral flow gradients in a lateral flow model.
NLDAS-2 forcing (12 km, 1980-2018) would provide spatially varying climate inputs across the basin, but this does not enable lateral flow.
open_questions: Is the intent to develop a lateral flow capability for this framework, or to redirect this question to an existing ParFlow/PFLOTRAN setup?
Would a simplified 1-D column set across hillslope positions (showing vertical partitioning differences) be of any value as a precursor, even though it does not answer the travel time question?
Are there existing ParFlow-CONUS or PFLOTRAN-CONUS runs for the Naches that could be leveraged?
Is there interest in a conceptual/idealized hillslope experiment (e.g. a synthetic 2-D hillslope transect in ParFlow) as a proof-of-concept before scaling to the full Naches domain?
